title: Quant sprint captures — 2-week run
content:
Sprint context and goals:
- Two-week mini-sprint to triage quantization regressions on rw-open-13b variant used in Dedicated tests.
- Primary goals: reproduce accuracy/latency gap, iterate on GPTQ/PACT-style configs, get a reliable baseline (FP16) + 4-bit and 8-bit comparisons, and create a short checklist for production rollout.

Day 0 — kickoff (2026-01-15):
- Quick notes from sync with Jay/Noah: prioritize throughput for batching workloads (avg seq 256) and keep tail latency <= 220ms p95 on A100-40GB.
- Eval set: 600 prompts (mix of instruction-following + retrieval-style). Will add 100 long-context prompts (2k tokens) on day 3.

Quick checklist (high priority):
- [ ] Reproduce FP16 baseline locally (torch 2.1, cuda 12.1)
- [ ] Run GPTQ 4-bit (group-size 128) and collect logits/EM/ROUGE diff against FP16
- [ ] Measure p50/p95 token latency and memory footprint for both streaming and non-streaming requests
- [ ] Instrument NVTX + Triton kernel traces for top-3 slow ops
- [ ] Add automated eval harness: save model outputs + per-prompt scores

Experiment notes (running configs tried so far):
1) Baseline FP16 (reference):
   - command: python run_eval.py --model ./models/rw-open-13b/fp16 --batch 4 --seq 256 --dtype float16
   - result: avg perplexity 12.6, EM-style QA 71.4, p95 token latency (A100) = 198ms, mem=17.8GB

2) GPTQ 8-bit (group=128, sym):
   - command: python quantize_gptq.py --model fp16 --out gptq-8g128 --bits 8 --group-size 128 --symmetric
   - notes: quantizer script uses calibration on 2k random sequences; observed small inflection on adversarial prompts
   - result: perplexity 13.1 (+4%), EM 69.9 (-1.5), p95=175ms, mem=10.5GB

3) GPTQ 4-bit (group=128, per-channel):
   - command: python quantize_gptq.py --bits 4 --group-size 128 --out gptq-4g128-pc --per-channel
   - result: perplexity 15.9 (+26%), EM 62.1 (-9.3), p95=160ms, mem=6.9GB
   - observation: quality drop exceeds acceptable threshold for some prompt classes (multi-step reasoning).

4) PTQ int8 asymmetric (baseline quick test):
   - result: perplexity 13.5, EM 68.5, p95=170ms
   - notes: int8 gave better accuracy than 4-bit GPTQ but worse memory reduction.

Prompt engineering notes (examples to include in eval harness):
- System: "You are a concise assistant that reasons step-by-step when asked to solve multi-step problems."
- Template A (QA): "Question: {q}
Answer:"
- Template B (chain-of-thought trigger): "Explain your reasoning before the final answer.
Q: {q}
A:"
- Observation: 4-bit models degrade disproportionately on Template B. Probable cause: quantization noise amplifies reasoning chain instability.

Profiling snippets to run next:
- nvprof / Nsight sampling to identify kernels with >20% time.
- torch.profiler with CPU/GPU activities and shapes captured. Use schedule: warmup=2, active=10, repeat=1.
- Enable aten fuser logs for matmul paths.

Immediate action items (next 48h):
- [ ] Rerun GPTQ 4-bit with group-size 64 and group-size 256 (compare group granularity effect)
- [ ] Try out GPTQ with activation smoothing (clip outliers) -> script flag --act-smooth=0.02
- [ ] Run eval on long-context set (2k tokens) to measure context scaling impact
- [ ] Add deterministic seed + save random_indices used for calibration so runs are reproducible

Failing prompt examples (to triage):
- prompt id 137: multi-step algebra, FP16 correct, 4-bit returns hallucinated formula
- prompt id 322: retrieval-verification, 4-bit gives wrong citation order (likely numeric precision)
- Plan: instrument per-layer activation norms during inference for these prompts.

Hypotheses and quick experiments: 
- H1: Poor scaling of KV-cache precision in 4-bit path causing gradual drift; test by forcing KV cache in FP16 while weights 4-bit (hybrid run).
- H2: Group-size too large causing coarse quantization; test group=32,64,128,256 and compare per-layer RMSE against FP16.
- H3: Outlier-aware quantization (RMS+clip) reduces hallucinations; add clip param and re-eval.

Commands to reproduce common runs (copyable):
- Quantize 4-bit (gptq): python quantize_gptq.py --model ./models/rw-open-13b/fp16 --out ./models/quant/gptq-4g128 --bits 4 --group-size 128 --per-channel --calib-samples 2000
- Eval harness: python run_eval.py --model ./models/quant/gptq-4g128 --evalset ./evals/mixed-600.json --batch 4 --seq 256 --track-diff ./logs/gptq-4g128-diff.json
- Serve quick local (single A100): torchrun --nproc_per_node=1 serve.py --model ./models/quant/gptq-4g128 --tensor-parallel 1 --streaming True

Notes for production rollout (criteria):
- Quality: EM within 3% absolute of FP16 on main eval set and no more than 10% degradation on chain-of-thought subset.
- Latency: p95 token latency <= 220ms (A100), p50 <= 80ms
- Cost: memory reduction must enable 2x density (2 models per node) for target savings to be meaningful.

Open questions / decisions needed from team:
- Can we accept a mixed-precision serving path (weights 4-bit, kv-cache FP16) in Redwood Dedicated? Security/compat implications?
- Is there appetite to add an automated calibration dataset (2k samples) to the onboarding flow for customers who want quantized variants?

Misc quick scratches (notes to self):
- Try re-compiling custom attention kernels with --use_fast_math off for verification.
- Follow up with infra: request A100-80GB smoke instance for long-context tests.
- Save intermediate outputs (logits) for failing prompts to /tmp/quant_debug/<run-id> for inspection.

End-of-sprint deliverables (draft):
- Short doc: "Quant tradeoffs for rw-open-13b" (1 pager) summarizing best config and rollout checklist.
- PR to serving repo for a hybrid-precision flag + e2e tests.
- Notebook with per-layer RMSE, latency curves, and failing prompt examples (attach to CONFLUENCE-ML-4821).

-- Hannah
(brief, messy notes; will tidy into a formal runbook after reproductions are stable)
